replication.target_description: Immediate RMET literary fiction versus nonfiction condition effect in mixed model controlling ART and ART × condition, text nested in experiment and condition; pooled replication comparison on page 5.

n.sample_role: Participants in the two final mutually exclusive comparison conditions; analytic sample for the identified mixed-model comparison. Text and experiment are modeled random effects, not participant counts.
n.exclusions: Final post-exclusion participants. Page 3 lists 510 additional recruits excluded for dropping out before text assignment (46), nonoriginal texts (165), noncompletion (284; superscript footnote 1 attached in canonical text), extreme reading times (3), low RMET outlier (1), and high ART guessing (10). These are whole-source exclusion counts, not separately allocated to this comparison; subgroup exclusion details are in unsupplied Tables S5/S6.

reported_success.quote: we found no support for any short-term ... causal effects of reading literary fiction on theory of mind.

notes: Identity verified from the supplied full primary replication article: matching title, all seven authors and DOI 10.1037/pspa0000064 on page 1; nine text pages include Methods, Results, Discussion and References. Header has provisional volume/issue/pagination (Vol. 111, No. 9, 000), unlike the final bibliographic issue, but title/authors/DOI identify the work. No PDF was supplied. Original source and unassigned fields were not examined; their schema entries are placeholders. Target matched by the immediate RMET outcome, named comparator, page locator and source methods (not numerical matching or row order). Page 4 explicitly reports this comparison N, so no N derivation was used. Page 4 defines the reported d as adjusted mean difference divided by model root mean square error. Page 7 Table 3 also gives a different pooled descriptive d; retained the page-located adjusted mixed-model d and its same-test p.  Reported_success refers to the authors’ paper-level verdict on immediate reading effects, not to the significant lifetime ART association.
